pathways.climate_pressure: Cyclone Ditwah flooding and landslides during the November 2025-January 2026 emergency.
pathways.documented_impact: Displacement and damaged access routes increased dependence on temporary shelters and disrupted assistance.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Crowding, insufficient lighting and privacy, shared sanitation and gaps in accessible protection services raised exposure to harm.
pathways.possible_consequence: Heightened gender-based violence risk reported by UNFPA; no measured cyclone-attributable incidence.
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing inequalities, household resources and service quality also influence protection risk.
Agency reporting is not an incident-based causal evaluation.
pathways.uncertainty: This is a source-stated post-disaster protection-risk mechanism, not proof of increased violence incidence, anthropogenic attribution of the cyclone, or a national FCV classification.
resilience_factors: Accessible shelters, privacy, lighting, sanitation and functioning protection referrals can address the reported risk factors; effectiveness is not evaluated.
pathways.compact_statement: Post-Ditwah shelter conditions and protection-service gaps heightened GBV risk; incidence changes were not measured.

executive_assessment.text: The assessment distinguishes post-conflict Mullaitivu and Batticaloa livelihood sensitivities and district-specific inclusive adaptation recommendations.
Land grievances, perceived allocation inequity and flood-related protection risks are source-stated mechanisms, with January 2026 shelter evidence; none is a national causal estimate.
Post-Ditwah shelter conditions and protection-service gaps heightened GBV risk; incidence changes were not measured.
